# Paired feature-group effects on the test period (generated by `scripts/analyze_ablation_ci.py`)

MAE of the second configuration minus the first, in MW (negative = adding the group helps); 95% moving-block bootstrap interval (block 168 h). Same hyper-parameters in every XGBoost configuration (tuned for S4), so the comparison is at a fixed model budget but not separately tuned per set. Intervals that include zero mean the effect is not distinguishable from zero on this single test year.

| step | 1 h | 6 h | 24 h | 48 h |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| calendar features (S0 -> S1) | -38 (-50 to -26; -3.4%) | -373 (-448 to -296; -12.0%) | -506 (-618 to -387; -11.8%) | -576 (-778 to -369; -10.0%) |
| holiday / festival features (S1 -> S2) | +1 (-8 to +10; +0.1%) | -32 (-109 to +32; -1.2%) | -78 (-208 to +37; -2.1%) | -56 (-270 to +113; -1.1%) |
| past observed weather (S2 -> S3) | +11 (-3 to +22; +1.0%) | +11 (-39 to +66; +0.4%) | +8 (-57 to +80; +0.2%) | -18 (-101 to +65; -0.3%) |
| past solar and wind (S3 -> S4) | +11 (+6 to +17; +1.0%) | +30 (-7 to +75; +1.1%) | +15 (-37 to +78; +0.4%) | +19 (-99 to +127; +0.4%) |
| ORACLE weather at the target hour (S4 -> S5; not available in reality) | -0 (-4 to +4; -0.0%) | -17 (-46 to +9; -0.6%) | -219 (-308 to -151; -5.9%) | -594 (-854 to -339; -11.5%) |
| LSTM: history+calendar -> full features (L1 -> L4) | +116 (+75 to +153; +7.6%) | +189 (+48 to +308; +6.3%) | -10 (-140 to +85; -0.3%) | +45 (-203 to +181; +0.8%) |

## How far do the inputs move outside the training range?

| variable | training max | share of validation hours above it | share of test hours above it | mean: train / validation / test |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| demand (MW) | 238,096 | 0.4% | 0.1% | 172,452 / 195,853 / 193,102 |
| solar generation (MW) | 44,258 | 8.9% | 15.4% | 10,101 / 14,092 / 16,097 |
| wind generation (MW) | 38,910 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 7,724 / 7,928 / 9,384 |
| national temperature (C) | 39 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 26 / 27 / 26 |

A large share of test hours above the training maximum means tree models cannot have seen such values (a tree predicts a constant beyond its last split) and a recurrent network is extrapolating; this matters for solar, whose installed capacity keeps growing (15% of test hours exceed the training maximum, mean +59% against training). Demand itself rarely exceeds the training maximum (0.1% of test hours) although its mean level is about 12% higher than in training; the anchor-relative target absorbs that shift.
